brief: Kioxia's December guidance showed NAND price gains slowing from 70% to the mid-20s, which drove Sandisk down more than 11% on Friday despite a beat and 8-for-1 split. That sets up competing notes on High-Bandwidth Flash (HBF): Bernstein (Mark Newman) argues NAND stacked HBM-style could ease AI's memory wall, since training compute has grown roughly 5x per year since 2020 versus about 28% per year for GPU memory bandwidth, and MoE models like Kimi K3 (2.8 trillion total, about 50 billion active parameters) keep memory demand high even as compute per token falls. Bernstein models an HBF-to-NAND wafer trade ratio of about 6.5x versus about 3x for HBM, implying a sensitivity where 10-20% demand migration could lift wafer requirements 20-120%, projects 86.5-92.7% gross margins, and rates Sandisk Outperform with a $3,000 target against a $1,150 close. Goldman (Jim Schneider) separately sees a $40-150B TAM by 2030 and about 30% lower inference cost, favoring Sandisk, SK Hynix and Samsung over Micron. Both banks flag the same open condition: Nvidia has not endorsed HBF, and its announced Rubin, Rubin Ultra and Feynman GPUs do not include it.
